evidence.note: Establishes a baseline picture: runs the full suite, checks summaries, and enumerates all failures before starting fixes.
Segments failures by suite (c-testsuite, wacc, gcc-torture), showing a per-suite view of what remains rather than a single blob.
Repeated 'Score'/'Final score' re-runs after fixes throughout the whole arc — sustained aggregate pass-count tracking to confirm net progress.
'Confirm stable', 'Check if still builds', 'Confirm' — explicit regression/stability checks after significant changes, not just forward progress.
Every score check is followed by re-listing failures and viewing specific failing tests, using the failure set to choose the next target.

reasoning: The agent sustains an aggregate pass-count ledger across the entire build, re-running the full suite after essentially every fix, explicitly checking stability/regressions ('Confirm stable', 'Check if still builds'), and using enumerated failure lists — segmented by suite — to prioritize the next fix. This clearly exceeds anchor 5 (which only notices count drops) and reaches most of anchor 8 (current pass/fail picture, regression checks after changes, failure-driven prioritization). It falls short of 9–10 because monitoring is re-run/aggregate-driven with no maintained per-category ledger tracking newly-passing vs newly-broken tests after each change, and evidence is behavioral (action descriptions) rather than an explicit structured status artifact — placing it at a 7.
